rules: Interior views are 24 mm unless the entry says otherwise; no interior entry uses a lens under 24 mm (16 mm only if a 24 mm frame cannot hold a single subject; none needed so far).
A view declares ONE subject cluster so a 24 mm frame can hold it; wide rooms get several views instead of a 16 mm view.
reuse = camera, lighting and caption of the existing definition in villa_render.VIEWS are kept; room = camera chosen by render_views.choose at 24 mm.
covers = rooms the frame is meant to show; render_set.coverage() checks each against the camera's field of view on plan.
Exposure is the existing per-group lock (knowledge/exposure-groups.json); no view is boosted.

Lamp-state rule (RF, lead decision 2026-11-22): a view of a windowless space whose only daylight path is an open end (ray probe: 36 of 20 000 rays escape from x 12.5 m of the GF east hall, none from x >= 15 m) is rendered in the design's Evening scene with daylight off, because 2700 K lamps mixed with spill daylight read as a blue cast. tests/test_villa_render_daylight_leak.py holds each such view to <= 10 % daylight.
